blind_spots.blind_spot: Scalable Compute Platform hosts third-party 'hardware and software payloads' on-orbit with no mention of an accreditation path for DoD data.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The moment a DoD program (MDA SHIELD, SpaceWERX) wants to run classified or CUI workloads on shared orbital compute, someone needs an ATO/IL4-equivalent for that multi-tenant environment — same failure mode as any shared-infrastructure product that skips RMF until the contract stalls.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is optimizing for flight heritage and TOPS benchmarks, not for the accreditation process that gates actual DoD payload hosting.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "It provides a full Linux high-performance computing environment, so you can containerize and move terrestrial software workflows to the point where they're most effective: your satellite in orbit."

blind_spots.blind_spot: OTP-2B is built around 'Ka-band uplink/downlink' for a 248 TOPS compute node, implying a persistent, high-bandwidth ground link.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A contested space domain (the exact mission MDA SHIELD is for) assumes adversary jamming/ASAT threats to that link — DDIL-equivalent for space is denied/degraded satcom, and nothing in the product language addresses graceful degradation when Ka-band is contested.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: On-orbit compute is marketed as solving a bandwidth problem for data processing, but the tasking/telemetry link itself is still treated as always-available.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "deploy a Gen 3 SCP micro data center with 248 TOPS of AI compute and Ka-band uplink/downlink, designed for a 5-year operational life"

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention anywhere in the pack of who operates, trains on, or sustains this system inside a DoD SDA/missile-defense architecture — no CONOPS, no integration language with existing Space Force command-and-control.
blind_spots.operator_reality: SHIELD is a layered-defense IDIQ; winning the contract is not the same as an operator/advocacy chain above program level actually integrating Rogue's sensor fusion into live decision loops — 'operators loving the demo' isn't adoption, and there's zero public language showing they've thought past the award.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's public voice is investor/commercial-customer facing (missions, TOPS, flight heritage) rather than program-office facing.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Rogue Space Systems is pleased to announce that it has been awarded a contract for the Missile Defense Agency Scalable Homeland Innovative Enterprise Layered Defense (SHIELD)"

opener_hook: Rogue's SCP touts TRL 9 flight heritage and 248 TOPS on-orbit compute — has an ATO path for hosting DoD payloads been defined yet?
what_they_do: Builds autonomous orbital robots (Orbots) and an on-orbit compute platform (SCP) for payload hosting, space domain awareness, and in-space logistics.
